script: art/species-construction/author_face_subd_patch_v2.py (post-assembly step A-face-subd; replaces A-face, finish_face_assembled.py). v1 author_face_subd_patch.py is kept unedited for the earlier pin.
step: A-face-subd (kind post, added --after assembly; inputs asm=assembly and donor=F-bulk) and F-bulk (rebuild_face_features_field.py on H25 with specs/face-bulk-r10e.json, the round 22 donor, read only for its skin). A-face is not in the recipe; H29 and H30 stay as the bulk face of the head chain.
reused: finish_face_assembled.py, as a copy and not an import (it is a script that runs at import, and a toolsmith may not turn it into a module): the window cut and zipper (stitch, pinch repair, closed-solid checks), the Eye class (aperture plane fit, conformal globe front_y), globe and iris lens objects, mouth follow, face metrics and sweepScore, records. Replaced: the fine level set (tiles, orbit carve, lid fold, tuft and nose SDFs) is now the subdivided cage. The F-bulk donor cache head-2492 is reused.
method: One regular grid over the window (cage.cell .005) is warped into ring blocks: each eye is a block whose rectangular levels become scaled copies of the aperture ellipse inside and offset curves outside (eye.rings: the lid band loop whose offset follows eye.lid.bandPercent, rim, lid fold, blend); the nose is a block on the rounded-triangle pad outline with its corners pinned. Heights are set per loop (socket floor behind the globe, aperture loop edgeCover in front of the globe edge, ring rises, optional lateral opening of the lid rings); tufts, muzzle lobes, philtrum groove and nose wedge are analytic heights sampled at the cage vertices. Donor and assembled skin are read as ray heightfields (bicubic), the border band is projected onto the assembled skin, the cage is Catmull-Clark subdivided cage.levels times by Blender's subsurf modifier (aperture and pad loops creased, material per face inherited), and the quads go through the field tool's window stitch. The lid band and the nose pad are skin material faces; globes and irises are retained objects.

parameters.name: cage.cell / cage.levels
parameters.what: cage grid cell (head-local) and subdivision levels. Output spacing is cell/2^levels (.00125); levels 3 halves it again (about 1.1M quads, slower). A smaller cell needs the ring offsets to fit the gap between the nose pad and the eye (the build stops with 'cage block overlaps another block' otherwise).

parameters.name: window.xByZ / x / z / yCut / margin / fade
parameters.what: the replaced window; its half width by height (xByZ) follows the front-facing part of the face, because the cage is a front heightfield and cannot follow the steep cheek and chin sides. Features fade out over `fade` inside the window edge, so keep rings and tufts inside it.

parameters.name: eye.aperture.center / semi
parameters.what: the white of the eye (inner edge of the lid band), head-local, left eye; the right eye mirrors. The dark band lies OUTSIDE it, so the outer edge of the band is semi plus the band width (about .0088 at the sides, .0137 at the top at bandScale 1). R02.md measures the aperture at the band's outer edge, so subtract the band width. Verified to move: semi [.084,.116] with center [.1767,.0123] gave aperture width .0451 (from .0519) and gap over width 1.10 (from .955).

parameters.name: eye.lid.bandPercent / bandScale / bandMode
parameters.default: R02.md table (6.5 at the top to 1.4 at the lower inner corner) / 1.0 / skin
parameters.what: width of the band loop by angle as percent of the eye width, times bandScale (1.6 added 16 band faces and moved the rim mean from .0009 to .0007). bandMode skin makes the faces between the aperture loop and the band loop a skin material; strip keeps finish_face_assembled's separate shell strip on the globe.

parameters.name: eye.rings[] {offset|gap, rise, crease, byAngle}
parameters.default: band; +.003 rise .0016; +.0035 rise .0012 byAngle top-heavy; +.004 rise 0
parameters.what: concentric loops outward from the aperture edge: offset (absolute) or gap (beyond the loop inside), rise (outward height over the donor surface), crease weight, byAngle multiplier table (degrees from the top, + toward the outer corner). The first entry is the lid band loop. Add or remove entries to change the number of loops; the block grows with them.

parameters.name: eye.orbit.floorBehind / edgeCover / lateralOpenDeg / lateralCenterDeg / openFeather
parameters.what: socket floor behind the globe front; how far the aperture loop sits in front of the globe edge; the angular width of the opened lateral wall (the rim rises scale to zero over that sector so the globe is not walled in from the side; 80 builds and moves the rim means).

parameters.name: tufts.list[] {root, tip, length, widthRoot, thickRoot, lift}
parameters.default: two per side, as the baseline control
parameters.what: each tuft is a lens ridge (head-local, x mirrored); taperPower, taperExponent, thicknessExponent, tipRadius, sectionPower (.5 elliptical) and rootCap shape them. Heights are sampled at the cage vertices (.005) and subdivided, so tips are softer than the old SDF locks; lower cage.cell for sharper tips.

parameters.name: nose.pad {topZ, apexZ, halfWidth, cornerRadius, lift, rings, blendLevels, extendStep}
parameters.what: the baseline's rounded-triangle pad outline; the three corners are pinned vertices, the outline loop is creased, the faces inside are the nose material. nose.wedge {lead, center, half} pushes the muzzle tip forward (default 0); muzzle {lobeLift, philtrumDepth, ...} are the lobes and the philtrum groove (default 0).

checks.build: recipe.py candidate tool-R02.json (session 2, after the block-edge and nose fixes): A-face-subd on assembled-2811 -> assembled-2813 in 5.1 min under load (the script alone about 25 s). loop_tools check passes: one skin component, 0 non-manifold edges, 868,844 vertices (709,302 before), height and ground spread 0. Globes and irises are retained closed objects; the old head_nose_finish shell is removed.

checks.direction: Packet m02 to m05 against assembled-2811: oval eyes of the baseline size with a dark band ring outside the white (top over bottom 3.3 on the left eye and 4.0 on the right, R02.2 asks at least 2.5), conformal skin rim, two broad pointed tufts per side, nose pad on the skin, no slab, box edge or floating piece. A faint shading step along the inner edges of the eye blocks above the nose showed in the first packet; the last build samples the heightfields bicubically to remove it (see the verification note in the notes).
checks.sweep: recipe.py sweep does not handle post steps. Three variants of the starter were built directly with the script and compared on face-parts.json: aperture semi [.084,.116] center [.1767,.0123] (width .0451, gap over width 1.10, band faces 320, sweepScore -.97), lid.bandScale 1.6 (band faces 392, rim mean .0007), orbit.lateralOpenDeg 80 (rim mean .0008, max .0043). Builders tune with plan variants (set edits on A-face-subd).
checks.session2: Fixed in session 2: (a) faint vertical and horizontal shading steps along the eye-block edges came from the cell size jumping from .002 inside the block to .005 outside within two levels; cage.blendLevels 4 and cage.extendStep .0035 remove them (checked in eyes-front at a 5 to 95 percent contrast stretch). (b) the nose pad read as a D because the outline table was sampled by support direction, which puts no points on the flat sides, so the polar interpolation bulged the top edge .015 above topZ; the outline is now corner arcs plus densely sampled straight sides, and nose.pad.pinCorners (default true, spec false) can pin the three corners. The pad is now a rounded-corner triangle, top edge flat at topZ, about .066 wide by .036 tall, apex at apexZ.
checks.session3: recipe.py candidate (A-face-subd on assembled-2811 -> assembled-2821, 20 min under load): loop_tools check pass (1 component, 0 non-manifold edges, 868,807 vertices); seamsNew []; region shift R01 R03 R05 .0044 to .0046 are the face window straddling zones, R04 and below 0. Packet m04 crops: nose is a crisp flat-topped triangle wider than v1, cheek and jowl masses smooth with no ridge lines, side view unchanged otherwise.

notes: Limits for the first order. (1) The cage is a front heightfield: it cannot follow overhangs or the steep chin and cheek sides, so the window stays on the front-facing part (xByZ) and the border band is projected onto the assembled skin. (2) The nose pad is a rounded triangle about .066 wide and .036 tall, a little blunter at the apex than the baseline's; nose.pad.cornerRadius, halfWidth, apexZ and pinCorners are the levers. (3) The lid band reads as an almost uniform thin ring in the front view at bandScale 1; raise the byAngle contrast or the top widths. (4) R02.md values need the aperture semi reduced by the band width. (5) Output spacing is .00125 head-local (cell .005, 2 levels) against the field tool's .0008 voxel. (6) The tool carries a copy of finish_face_assembled.py's stitch code, so a fix there is not picked up here. (7) A post build still takes 5 to 20 minutes with the mesh export and renders. Round 28 fix pass: see reasonsFixed; tune tufts.* and nose.pad.* in the v2 spec.
reasonsFixed: Round 28 reader rejection (3-0 for the baseline: candidate nose narrower and rounder, small hard spiky tufts and faceted creases on the cheeks, lumps in the jowl). Causes found: (1) the tuft root cap profile was (1-(u/cap)^2)^.5, a vertical wall that read as a crease around each cheek tuft, and the section power .5 made the same wall along the tuft sides; v2 adds tufts.capPower (2.0) and sets sectionPower 2.0, tipRadius .012, taperExponent .6, thicknessExponent 1.3, thickRoot .008 and .007 so tufts are soft masses with zero slope at their edge. (2) The nose pad lost its corners: pinCorners was false and creaseNose .9, so Catmull-Clark rounded the triangle; v2 pins the corners, creases at 1.0, halfWidth .045 (was .043), apexZ -.152, cornerRadius .0045, ring offsets .002 and .004 (a wider pad with the old offsets overlaps the eye block; halfWidth .048 also overlaps, .003 radius folds).
